scenarios.title: Calendar layout and complete lunar dates
steps: Run the fixture command Chrono Notes acceptance provider: Prepare January 2029 calendar. This only positions the calendar; inspect and switch views through the product UI.

Inspect Month and Century at narrow and normal widths in light and dark appearance. In the narrow two-column Century layout, verify each decade header spans both year columns. Include January 2029, whose two-digit lunar month/day values must remain complete in narrow cells (wrapping is allowed). Inspect the complete lunar date in a desktop hover/focus preview.
expected: Selection and calendar content remain readable in both appearances and narrow layouts; narrow Century decade headers span both year columns, and complete lunar wording remains available in the desktop preview.

scenarios.title: Calendar note-opening gestures
steps: In English, open the month calendar and select a date. Verify compact numeric lunar text and no Enter glyph. Open its note with Enter on desktop or long press on touch; confirm note creation if requested.
expected: Lunar cells retain distinct month/day values, the selected cell has no persistent return glyph, and the platform's opening gesture works.

scenarios.title: Complete ICS day details without preview
steps: Run Chrono Notes acceptance provider: Prepare ICS source list. Enable the seeded sources through product settings and refresh; the first 32 sources have events on 2026-09-19.

Turn off calendar hover previews. Navigate to 2026-09-19 in the product calendar. On desktop open the date context menu with the keyboard and with a mouse; on Android open it by touch long press. Choose View calendar events.

Inspect the full list, scroll through its last items, verify event titles and source names, then close the modal with Escape or the native close control. Confirm focus and date navigation still work after closing. Disable ICS after the observation.
expected: The complete 32-event list is reachable with previews off and contains the last indexed source without truncation or a nested control. The modal remains readable and closable on both surfaces.

scenarios.title: ICS source errors and recovery
steps: Run Chrono Notes acceptance provider: Prepare ICS source list to restore the 35 local fixture sources with ICS disabled. Enable and refresh them through the product UI.

In Extensions and integrations, enable the 35 seeded ICS sources and refresh. Verify three omitted sources and zero read errors. Temporarily make the first source path invalid and refresh again; verify one real error and the same three omitted sources in both the notice and persistent status. Restore the path and refresh to clear the error.
expected: Source omissions do not inflate the read-error count, real errors remain visible alongside the warning, and a successful refresh clears the error.

scenarios.title: Arabic labels and complete feedback
steps: Run Chrono Notes acceptance provider: Prepare ICS source list to restore the 35 local fixture sources with ICS disabled. Enable and refresh them through the product UI.
Switch the interface to Arabic. Inspect the word-count statistic label and the periodic-note enabled label; verify that both are visible. Inspect ICS feedback for complete sentences. Restore English.
Disable ICS after the observation.
expected: The repaired Arabic labels and ICS sentences are non-empty and the tabbed settings remain usable.

scenarios.title: Periodic-note navigation and tabbed settings
steps: Open the Chrono workspace and navigate between the seeded daily and weekly notes
Open every settings tab and switch language between Follow Obsidian, English, and Simplified Chinese
Use the daily-note command and approve its preview to create today's note from the seeded template
expected: Calendar selection and periodic-note anchors remain consistent
The imperative tabbed settings surface remains complete and usable
Template creation is previewable and creates only the requested note

scenarios.title: Explicit and unmarked range-note recognition
steps: Open the Range notes settings tab and read the recognition guide and unmarked-note scope
Open the range-note list with the default range-folder scope
Create a range note and inspect its Properties
expected: The guide states that chrono-notes: interval is recognized across the Vault and that unmarked notes use the configured scope
The seeded explicit note outside the range folder and the unmarked note inside it are listed, while the seeded note with chrono-notes: daily is excluded
The new note contains chrono-notes: interval with canonical start and end properties

scenarios.title: Periodic paths keep their configured language
steps: Open the Periodic settings and inspect the separate path-language controls. Switch the interface between English and Simplified Chinese; verify that the configured path previews keep their filename language.

Configure daily [Daily]/YYYY-MMMM-DD, monthly [Monthly]/YYYY-MMMM and yearly [Yearly]/YYYY-MMMM with English path language and empty templates. Create a note for 2026-10-17, October 2026 and year 2026 through the product UI. Record their actual paths.

With the calendar still open, change only the relevant path language to Simplified Chinese. Inspect Month and Week for the daily note, Year for the monthly note, and Century for the yearly note: the English-path note becomes missing immediately. Switch back to English and verify the existing state returns without reopening the calendar.
Open the existing English-path notes from all four views, then change the interface language only and repeat. Confirm paths and file counts remain unchanged. Restore the original path rules.
expected: Changing interface language does not redirect configured paths; editing one period language does not change another period.
All four views refresh on pathLocale changes, open the correct existing note, and do not create duplicate files when only the interface language changes.

scenarios.title: Partial periodic-note creation preserves successes
steps: Enable larger-period cascading, create a new daily note through its confirmation, and observe the one partial-success notice for the missing monthly template. Confirm the daily and yearly notes remain available. Disable larger-period cascading after the observation.
expected: Partial creation keeps success and failure distinguishable and preserves the successfully created files.

scenarios.title: ICS occurrence budget feedback
steps: Enable ICS with Calendars/Budget.ics and refresh. Inspect both the refresh notice and persistent settings summary for the 100,000-occurrence limit, omitted events and recovery advice; disable ICS afterwards.
expected: Budget omissions are explained to the user rather than reported only as an unspecified error.

scenarios.title: Century selection, focus and gestures
steps: Open the calendar Century view. Select a rightmost-column year and inspect its complete outline and scrollbar clearance in light and dark appearance, a narrow pane and enlarged interface text.

On desktop, navigate with Tab, arrows, Home/End and Enter. On touch, select and long-press a year. Verify that selection and focus frames do not cover the year or status information, no Enter/return glyph is drawn inside the selected cell, and Today remains identifiable.
expected: Century selection and focus outlines remain visible beside the scrollbar, controls remain readable, and normal opening gestures work.

scenarios.title: Task writes preserve closed and open note content
steps: Open the calendar at 2026-09-19 and switch to Week. Toggle Boundary task from BOM Tasks.md while its source is closed, then open the source and verify the checkbox and unchanged surrounding text.

Keep the task source open in an editor, add a sentinel line, and toggle the task from the calendar again. Verify the task changes and the sentinel survives. Timing races are covered separately by automated adapter tests.
expected: Closed and open task updates persist the intended checkbox without changing surrounding text or reporting a false failure.

scenarios.title: Localized ICS source limits and recovery
steps: Run Chrono Notes acceptance provider: Prepare ICS source list to restore the 35 local fixture sources with ICS disabled. Enable and refresh them through the product UI.

In Extensions and integrations, enable the 35 seeded ICS sources and refresh. Verify the notification and persistent settings explain the limit of 32, three omitted sources, and how to reduce or reorder sources.
Switch the interface to Simplified Chinese, return to ICS settings and refresh. Verify the same source-limit explanation is localized.
Replace the source list with Calendars/Sources/01.ics and Calendars/Sources/02.ics, refresh, and verify both sources load with no stale omission warning.
expected: The first 32 sources load and the three omitted sources are explicitly explained in both notification and settings, in English and Simplified Chinese.
Reducing the source list clears the omission warning and loads all remaining sources.

scenarios.title: Real Templater periodic and range creation
steps: Install and enable a released Templater plugin in the isolated test Vault, record its version, and disable automatic folder templates to prevent double rendering. If Templater is unavailable, record unverified, not passed.

Select Templater as the Chrono Notes template engine and Templates/Templater Context.md. Create a daily note for 2026-10-17 through the calendar confirmation. Inspect the result: kind=periodic, title matching the destination, target=2026-10-17 and no remaining template delimiters.
Use the same template for a range note from 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-19. Verify kind=interval, start/end dates, dayCount=3, destination title and canonical interval identity.

Select Templates/Templater Failure.md and create another note. Verify an actionable localized rendering error and preservation of the created target. Then configure a missing template, retry with a different destination, and verify no target was created.

Restore the working template, enable larger-period cascading with a missing monthly template, create a fresh daily note, and verify one partial-success notice plus preserved daily/yearly successes. Restore settings.
expected: Real Templater renders in create-note mode against the actual target file; selected dates and range boundaries are correct. Failures and partial success remain distinct and never erase successful files.

scenarios.title: Complex Markdown task writeback
steps: Open Week at 2026-10-17 with Complex Tasks.md closed. Verify Ordered task and Callout task are listed; Comment-only task and Code-only task are absent.

Toggle Ordered task, then reschedule it to 2026-10-18 through the calendar. Inspect the file: only its checkbox and visible due date change; the hidden 2000-01-01 date, ordered marker and surrounding lines remain byte-equivalent.

Keep Complex Tasks.md open, append a sentinel using the editor and immediately toggle Callout task from the calendar. Verify the sentinel survives along with the callout prefix, inline code and comments. Reschedule the callout and verify only its visible date changes.

Undo the intended edits through normal controls and confirm no duplicate tasks or hidden-date ghosts appear. Record original and resulting file bytes; timing races remain separately covered by automated adapter tests.
expected: Task indexing excludes comments/code; writes preserve Markdown containers, hidden dates and unrelated live edits.

scenarios.title: RTL calendar keyboard and focus
steps: Switch the interface to Arabic, then repeat in Persian and Hebrew. Focus a middle Month date with adjacent cells on both sides. ArrowRight moves to the visually right neighbor (previous date); ArrowLeft returns. Home/End and Enter preserve visible focus and normal opening behavior.

Open the week picker and test ArrowRight/ArrowLeft between adjacent weeks. Inspect Year heatmap and Century navigation, and the date picker modal: keyboard movement follows visual direction, focus stays visible and closing restores usable calendar navigation.
Inspect all five settings tabs at narrow and normal widths. Restore English and confirm LTR keyboard movement returns.
expected: RTL direction, keyboard movement and focus are consistent across calendar surfaces, popovers and modal controls; settings remain usable.

scenarios.title: Gregorian localized month identity and settings focus after saving
steps: Select Persian, inspect a known Gregorian month in the calendar and open one date; verify label and selected note refer to the same Gregorian date.

Open the final settings tab, change a calendar or holiday control twice, and verify saved values and active-tab visibility after each rebuild. On desktop verify keyboard focus returns to the replacement control.
Repeat a representative setting change in English, check the guide and problem-report entries and inspect narrow RTL layout.
expected: Localized language and digits retain Gregorian date identity.
Saving preserves values and keeps the active settings tab visible.
Desktop focus and mobile narrow controls remain usable.
